title: Integers
description: Class 7 IMO — Integers: properties (closure, commutative, associative, distributive, identity, inverse), all four operations, and word problems on temperature, elevation and bank balance.

topics.title: Properties of Integers
topics.concept:
Integers are closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. Addition and multiplication are commutative and associative, and multiplication is distributive over addition.

The additive identity is 0 (a + 0 = a) and the multiplicative identity is 1 (a × 1 = a). The additive inverse of a is −a, since a + (−a) = 0.

examples.problem: What is the additive identity for integers?
examples.solution: 0, because adding 0 leaves a number unchanged.

examples.problem: What is the additive inverse of 7?

recap: Commutative and associative for + and ×; distributive of × over +.
Additive identity 0, multiplicative identity 1, additive inverse of a is −a.

quiz.q: What is the multiplicative identity for integers?
quiz.explanation: Multiplying by 1 leaves a number unchanged, so 1 is the multiplicative identity.
A number plus its additive inverse is 0.

topics.title: Operations on Integers
topics.concept:
Integers are whole numbers that can be positive (+), negative (-), or zero. Think of a number line as your main tool for visualizing integer operations.

Rules for addition:

  • Same sign: add absolute values and keep the sign. Example: (-3) + (-4) = -7
  • Different signs: subtract absolute values and keep the sign of the number with the larger absolute value. Example: (-8) + (+3) = -5

Rule for subtraction: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite.

Example: 5 - (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8

examples.solution: Same sign: 8 + 6 = 14, keep the sign, so −14.

examples.problem: A scuba diver is at -12 feet. She rises 7 feet. Where is she now?
The temperature at 6 AM was -8 degrees C. By noon it rose 15 degrees C. What is the noon temperature?
A bank account has -$20 (overdraft). You deposit $50. What is the new balance?

recap: Subtracting an integer = adding its opposite.
Like signs → positive; unlike signs → negative.
Positive + Negative = sign of bigger absolute value
To subtract: change minus to plus, flip the sign of the second number

topics.title: Word Problems with Integers
topics.concept: Integers describe real situations: a temperature rise is positive and a fall is negative, height above sea level is positive and depth below is negative, and a bank deposit is positive while an overdraft is negative.

examples.problem: The temperature is −3°C and rises by 8°C. What is the new temperature?
A bank balance is −₹500 (overdrawn). After depositing ₹800, what is the balance?

recap: Combine with integer addition and subtraction.

questions.q: Which property does a + b = b + a show?
questions.explanation: Changing the order without changing the result is the commutative property.

questions.q: a + 0 = a shows that the additive identity is ___ ?
questions.explanation: Adding 0 leaves a unchanged, so 0 is the additive identity.
−3 is to the right of −8, so it is greater.
Same sign: 7 + 5 = 12, keep the sign, so −12.
